chunks: Design a high-side NFET drive. The question: Design a circuit to properly drive a high-side NFET. What considerations must be taken into account?

A high-side NFET (an N-type transistor in the top position, between the input and the switch node) needs its gate about 5 volts above its source, but its source is the switch node, which swings up to the input voltage.
So the gate driver needs a supply that rides up and down with the switch node.
The standard solution is a bootstrap capacitor, charged while the node is low and carried upward when the node rises.
Picture a person standing on a lift, carrying a battery lantern. At the bottom they plug the lantern into the wall to charge it.
When the lift rises, they carry the charged lantern with them and keep their light on, even though the wall is far below. The bootstrap capacitor is that carried battery.
The driver's high-side channel runs from BST to SW, powered by C boot .
D boot charges the cap from V DRV while SW is low (low side on, or its body diode conducting) and blocks when SW rises.
C boot connects from BST to the switch node, so it floats with SW; HO drives Q 1 's gate relative to that same node. Q 2 is driven directly from the driver's LO output.
Bootstrap capacitor: a capacitor that stores the gate-drive voltage and floats with the switch node. Gate driver: a circuit that charges and discharges the gate quickly.
Gate charge ( Q g ): the charge needed to turn the transistor on. Switch node: the point whose voltage swings from ground to the input.
Maximum duty cycle: the limit set by needing time to recharge the capacitor.
A transistor needs 12 nC of gate charge, and we allow the bootstrap voltage to droop by 0. 3 volts. The capacitor must be at least 12 nC over 0. 3 volts equals 40 nanofarads.
In practice we pick 100 nanofarads to leave margin. It recharges only when the switch node goes low. That is the whole idea.
"The high-side NFET's source is the switch node, so its gate has to go to V in plus about 5 volts.
I'd use a bootstrap: a gate driver whose supply pin is a capacitor from BST to SW, charged through a Schottky from a 5 volts rail while the low side is on.
Size it as C at least Q g over change in V , for example 12 nC over 0. 3 volts is 40 nanofarads, then use 100 nanofarads.
Considerations: refresh limits max duty, pre-biased start-up, SW undershoot and dv/dt immunity, edge control with a gate or boot resistor, dead time, and tight layout."
Quick check. Why can't a high-side NFET be driven from a ground-referenced 5 volts logic signal directly?
